statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107888 (GHSA-qqm8-4q5h-jg55): OpenPrinting CUPS before 2.4.20 dereferences a NULL pointer in cupsdCheckJobs() when a job held on create refers to a temporary printer that has since been deleted, which terminates cupsd. It is fixed in CUPS 2.4.20: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-qqm8-4q5h-jg55, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-107888. The DHI cups packages for Alpine 3.23 are published at 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0, 2.4.18-r0 and 2.4.18-r1 (x86_64 and aarch64). 2.4.13-r0, 2.4.16-r0 and 2.4.18-r0 are builds of those CUPS releases with Alpine's packaging, published before the advisory and without any backport for it, so they are affected. 2.4.18-r1 is built from CUPS 2.4.18 with a backport of the upstream fix for CVE-2026-107888, so it is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-107888 (GHSA-qqm8-4q5h-jg55): OpenPrinting CUPS before 2.4.20 dereferences a NULL pointer in cupsdCheckJobs() when a job held on create refers to a temporary printer that has since been deleted, which terminates cupsd. It is fixed in CUPS 2.4.20: https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/security/advisories/GHSA-qqm8-4q5h-jg55, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-107888. Debian lists trixie's 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107888). DHI publishes four rebuilds of Debian's cups 2.4.10-3+deb13u2 for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64). Read the Debian changelog shipped in each of their cups-daemon packages: the first does not list CVE-2026-107888; the second is the first to record the backport of the upstream fix, and the third and fourth keep it. The second rebuild is the fixed version in this range; every earlier build, including the earlier rebuilds no longer in the repository, which predate the backport, is affected.
